messages:
Maria Chen: OK team, I'm handing off the evening shift — I'm primary until 17:45 UTC then Kevin will take over. Leaving a quick runbook pointer and coverage note.

Maria Chen: Current state: a few customers seeing increased tail latency on hosted/text-gen in us-west-2. No full outages, errors ~0.3% (normal is 0.05%). I've opened a Sev2 for now: INC-2026-034.

Maria Chen: Primary -> Maria Chen (me) until 17:45 UTC. Secondary -> Kevin Patel. Ben is oncall-lead fallback. Pager escalation order is in the runbook below.

Incident Bot: New incident INC-2026-034 created by Maria Chen. Severity: Sev2. Affected product: hosted/text-gen (us-west-2). Links: https://incidents.redwood.local/INC-2026-034.

Kevin Patel: Got it — taking over at 17:45. Any active mitigations?

Maria Chen: Yes — I've throttled the burst pool for the text-gen route (route: /v1/generate-text) and enabled short-circuit fallback to the smaller model (redwood-small-v2) for non-high-priority keys. That dropped the token CPU for the top 5 pods.

Maria Chen: Notes for you @Kevin: the customer-facing dashboard for affected customers is here: https://internal.redwood/observability/customers/latency-dashboard. Check token tail latency metric (tail_99_9) and the batching queue depth.

Priya Singh: Quick Q on escalation: if this worsens to >1% errors or any customer-facing timeouts, do we page infra-sre or product-ops first?

Ben (oncall-lead): Page infra-sre immediately for platform-impacting perf degradations. Product-ops only if a committed SLA is at risk or if a customer escalates to CSM. For anything that looks like a model runtime bug (OOMs, mem spikes) page eng-runtime.

Kevin Patel: Understood. Can we get the paging matrix here for reference? I didn't find the newest one in the runbook.

Maria Chen: Paste of the quick paging matrix (from /runbooks/oncall-paging):
```
Sev0/P0: page primary -> primary pager + call, then oncall-lead + exec-ops if no ack in 60s
Sev1/P1: page primary pager, if no ack in 5m -> secondary pager, after 10m -> oncall-lead
Sev2: page primary Slack mention + incident channel, escalate to infra-sre within 15m if platform metrics keep degrading
Customer-visible outage: product-ops + CSM + legal if >1hr
```

Sam W: Small note: our pager system uses PagerDuty -> phone fallthrough after 3 tries. If pager fails, call the phone numbers listed on the rotation doc.

Priya Singh: Thanks. For this particular incident, what's the 'when to escalate' threshold concretely?

Maria Chen: For INC-2026-034 specifically: escalate to infra-sre if any of the following happen in the next 15m:
- tail_99_9 for text-gen > 2s for 5 consecutive minutes
- error rate > 1% for 3 consecutive minutes
- CPU on inference hosts > 85% sustained for 2 min
If any of those hit, page infra-sre (pager: infra-sre@pager) and ping @Ben.

Kevin Patel: I'll watch metrics. If we need infra-sre, I'll page and annotate the incident with timestamps. Also will try a quick rolling restart of the top-most noisy pod if CPU stays high (per runbook step 4).

Maria Chen: Yes, follow small-batch rolling restart (runbook step 4) and only restart one replica at a time. Command I used earlier (copy):
```
kubectl -n inference set image deployment/text-gen-pool text-gen=text-gen:v3-rollback && kubectl rollout status deploy/text-gen-pool -w
```

Priya Singh: If someone pages infra-sre, what's their expected response SLA?

Ben (oncall-lead): infra-sre ack within 10m for Sev1/P1, within 5m for Sev0/P0. For this Sev2, we expect an ack within 15m, and a remediation plan within 30m. If not met, bump to oncall-lead and exec-ops.

Incident Bot: Alert: metric tail_99_9 has spiked to 1.8s for hosted/text-gen in us-west-2 at 17:12:06 UTC.

Maria Chen: Thanks bot — tracking. Kevin, looks like we're inching up. I'm going to leave detailed notes in the incident: mitigation toggles, steps tried, and which customer keys saw the errors.

Kevin Patel: I initiated a controlled throttle reduction at 17:16 UTC (reduced concurrency for guest keys). Will monitor. If no improvement by 17:25, I'll escalate to infra-sre.

Sam W: Reminder for handoff: when you swap, update the oncall doc with the brief "state" line and the time you swapped. Also add any unmerged config changes to the PR checklist to avoid surprises for the next shift.

Maria Chen: Done — state updated and PRs linked. Passing to @Kevin at 17:45. If anything critical happens before then, page as per matrix. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Kevin Patel: Taking over now. I'm primary. I will post another status update in 20 minutes or sooner if things change.

Ben (oncall-lead): Thanks both. If the incident escalates beyond infra-sre's scope, dispatch the outage bridge and tag @exec-ops.

Incident Bot: Incident INC-2026-034 status changed to "monitoring" at 17:40:20 UTC.

Kevin Patel: Update 17:50 UTC — metrics trending down after throttle and fallback to redwood-small-v2. tail_99_9 at 1.0s, errors back to 0.4%. I'm keeping primary and will keep watching for 30 more minutes.

Maria Chen: Awesome — thanks for the handoff notes. If you want a quick walkthrough of recent kernel flags I toggled, ping me in DMs.
